heroSub: Door-to-door auto transport for the Capital Region, dispatched from 111 Washington Ave downtown. Open and enclosed carriers, instant online quotes, and pickups that take advantage of the Northway and Thruway traffic rolling through Exit 24 every day.
intro:
Car shipping from Albany is easier than most people expect, and the reason is geography. The I-87 Northway meets the I-90 Thruway at Exit 24 on the west side of the city, which makes the Capital Region the crossroads for nearly every car hauler moving between New England, Montreal, New York City and the Midwest. Those trucks already pass through Albany, so a pickup in Pine Hills, Delmar or Latham rarely means waiting for a special trip. Our office at 111 Washington Ave #1750, a few blocks from the State Capitol and Empire State Plaza, books Albany auto transport for state employees, university families, Albany Med residents and the growing Tech Valley workforce.

We are a New York based, FMCSA licensed broker: we vet the carriers, hold them to insurance requirements and manage the schedule. Open and enclosed trailers are both available, door to door, anywhere in the lower 48. Whether you are a legislator heading home after the June session, a retiree leaving Loudonville for Florida or a GlobalFoundries engineer arriving from Austin with a car that needs to follow you, we can move it. Call (518) 535-3703 or run an instant quote online.

sections.h2: Why Exit 24 makes Albany an easy pickup
sections.html:
Most of the Northeast's long-haul car carriers run one of two corridors. The Thruway carries them east and west between Boston, the Berkshires, Buffalo and Chicago. The Northway and I-787 carry them north and south between Montreal, Plattsburgh, Saratoga and the New York City metro. Both corridors hit Albany, and the toll plaza at Exit 24 is where they cross. A carrier running Boston to Chicago can swing into Guilderland or Colonie, load a sedan, and be back on I-90 in twenty minutes.

That traffic is why pickup windows out of the Capital Region are usually one to four days once a vehicle is dispatched, with Florida and Carolina loads typically filling the fastest. Rensselaer, East Greenbush and Troy on the east side of the Hudson are just as convenient for carriers crossing on I-90. Cohoes, Watervliet and Menands sit right along I-787, so a hauler coming down from the North Country can stop without leaving the highway corridor.

sections.h2: Where Albany car haulers actually meet you
sections.html:
A 75-foot nine-car trailer does not belong on Lark Street or State Street. Downtown Albany is a maze of one-ways, the state garages under the Plaza have clearance limits, and the Empire State Plaza concourse is not a loading zone. If you live or work in Center Square, Arbor Hill, Delaware Ave or near the Capitol, expect the driver to ask you to meet somewhere with room to swing a trailer.

  • Crossgates Mall in Guilderland, right off Exit 24 and Washington Ave Extension, is the most common meeting point for the whole region.
  • Colonie Center and the Wolf Rd retail strip are a close second, especially for customers in Latham, Loudonville and Colonie.
  • Albany International Airport long-term lots work well for anyone flying out the same day their car ships.
  • Central Ave (Route 5) plazas and the big-box lots along Route 9 in Latham and Route 20 in Guilderland all have the turning radius a hauler needs.

Delmar, Slingerlands and Glenmont customers usually meet at a plaza on Delaware Ave or Route 9W. Buckingham Pond, Whitehall and New Scotland Ave are residential enough that curbside pickup often works if the street is wide.

sections.h2: State workers, session staff and Albany's campuses
sections.html:
Albany's moving calendar is unlike anywhere else in New York. The Legislature is in session from January through June, and we see a steady stream of staffers, lobbyists and members who keep a car here for the session and want it sent back to Long Island, Rochester or Buffalo when the budget finally passes. State agency transfers run year round, and a civil servant moving from the Harriman campus to a regional office in Syracuse or Hauppauge usually has a two-week window to relocate everything, car included.

The campuses add their own rhythms. SUNY Albany's uptown campus on Washington Ave fills in late August and empties in May, and parents in Westchester or on Long Island often ship a student's car rather than make the drive twice. Albany Law and Siena in Loudonville follow a similar pattern. Albany Medical Center brings in a new class of residents every July, many from out of state, and a good share of them need a car hauled from Texas, California or the Midwest to a Pine Hills apartment. Across the river, RPI in Troy sends graduates to engineering jobs in Boston, Seattle and the Bay Area every spring, and we handle a lot of those one-way moves.

sections.h2: Moving in for Tech Valley jobs
sections.html:
The Capital Region's growth story is inbound, not just outbound. GlobalFoundries in Malta, the nanotech corridor along Fuller Rd and Washington Ave Extension, and Regeneron's East Greenbush campus recruit engineers and scientists from Arizona, Texas, California and the Carolinas, and those hires typically fly in to start work while their car comes up separately. If you are landing in Latham, Clifton Park or East Greenbush for one of these jobs, the best move is to book the car a week or two before your flight so it arrives within a few days of you.

Inbound loads to Albany are priced on the same corridors as outbound ones, and because so many carriers run empty back up the Northway after dropping Florida snowbird cars in the fall, northbound rates from the Southeast can be a little softer in October and November. Corporate relocation packages often cover auto transport, and we can invoice the employer directly. The Port of Albany also handles roll-on roll-off cargo, and if you are coordinating an international vehicle move through the port, we can arrange the domestic leg to or from the terminal.

sections.h2: Albany winters: frozen cars, Northway salt and what counts as inoperable
sections.html:
Albany averages around 60 inches of snow a year and strings of nights well below zero in January and February. That matters for car shipping in two ways. First, a car that has sat in a Delmar driveway for three weeks and will not turn over because of a dead battery is, for transport purposes, inoperable. Carriers need a working winch or a tow to load a non-running car, and that adds roughly $150 to $250 to the rate. Tell us up front if the car is a hard starter so we dispatch a truck that can load it.

Second, the Northway and Thruway are salted heavily all winter, and an open carrier picks up the same brine your own car would on I-87. For a daily driver that is a non-issue, but for a clean low-mileage car heading south for the first time, an enclosed trailer avoids the salt spray entirely. Snow emergencies in the city also close parking on posted streets, so if a storm is forecast on pickup day, we will move the meeting to Crossgates or Colonie Center rather than fight the plows downtown.

sections.h2: Enclosed transport for Saratoga season and Capital Region collectors
sections.html:
Open carriers handle the great majority of Albany auto transport and are the right choice for a Subaru heading to Charlotte or a Honda going to a SUNY student in Buffalo. Enclosed demand here is seasonal and specific. Every August the Saratoga Race Course meet pulls owners, trainers and a fair number of collector cars into horse country north of the city, and the enclosed haulers that serve Saratoga Springs, Ballston Spa and Malta that month pass straight through Albany, which makes it an easy time to book covered transport for a vintage Porsche or a restored Corvette from Slingerlands or Loudonville.

Enclosed typically runs 40 to 60 percent above an open rate on the same lane, so Albany to Florida is roughly $1,150 to $1,350 enclosed versus $750 to $850 open. For most moves that premium is not worth it, but for a soft top, low ground clearance, fresh paint or a six-figure value, it is cheap insurance.

faqs.q: I live in Center Square and park on the street. Can a carrier pick up at my door?
faqs.a: Almost never. The blocks around Lark Street and Washington Park are too tight for a full-size car hauler, and there is nowhere legal to stage a trailer. The driver will usually ask you to meet at Crossgates Mall off Exit 24 or at Colonie Center on Wolf Rd. Both are fifteen minutes from downtown with room for a nine-car rig.

faqs.q: How far ahead should I book if the session ends and I need my car back downstate?
faqs.a: A week is comfortable. The end of the legislative session in June and the end of the SUNY Albany year in May are both busy, and short hauls to Long Island, Rochester or Boston move on carriers that fill quickly. Albany to Boston typically runs $350 to $450 and one to two days in transit.

faqs.q: My car has been sitting all winter in Latham and will not start. Can you still ship it?
faqs.a: Yes, but it ships as inoperable. The carrier needs a winch to load a car that does not run, and not every open trailer has one, so we assign a truck that does. Expect roughly $150 to $250 above the running rate. If a jump start or a new battery gets it running before pickup day, let us know and we can re-quote it as operable.

faqs.q: Which is cheaper for Albany to Florida, open or enclosed, and how long does it take?
faqs.a: Open is the budget option. A running sedan from Albany to Orlando or Tampa on an open carrier typically runs $750 to $850 and three to five days. Enclosed runs about $1,150 to $1,350 on the same lane. Carriers heading south from the Capital Region pick up the Thruway or Northway, drop to I-95 near New York and run straight down the coast.

faqs.q: I am relocating to the Capital Region for a GlobalFoundries job. Should I ship or drive from Phoenix?
faqs.a: Shipping usually wins once you count fuel, two or three nights of hotels and the vacation days a 2,500 mile drive burns. Phoenix to Albany on an open carrier is about $1,250 to $1,350 and six to eight days. Book it a week before you fly so the car arrives at your Malta or Clifton Park address within a few days of you, and ask your employer whether relocation covers the cost.
